fullText:
Alongside the usual bug fixes and performance improvements, macOS Tahoe 26.1 is rolling out right now. Here’s what’s new.

Here’s what’s new on macOS Tahoe 26.1

Following a few weeks of developer and public betas, macOS Tahoe 26.1 is rolling out right now, and it brings a couple of small user-facing features, as well as groundwork preparation for upcoming AI enhancements.

First, Apple has been working to add MCP support to macOS, iPadOS, and iOS. In a nutshell, MCP is an open standard developed by Anthropic, which allows AI models to interact with user-facing platforms and tools. Despite back-end changes to bring MCP support, Apple hasn’t publicly commented on when or how that will be integrated.

macOS Tahoe 26.1 also brings a few under-the-hood improvements to Image Playground, laying the groundwork for support of third-party image generation models beyond ChatGPT. Like with the MCP support, Apple hasn’t publicly commented on the upcoming extended support, but based on the code, this may happen sooner rather than later.

As for user-facing features, the highlight of macOS Tahoe 26.1 is a new option to either keep the standard Liquid Glass appearance or switch to a Tinted mode, which slightly adjusts the visuals to improve contrast. On macOS, the visual changes are subtle, but they become more noticeable on iPadOS and iOS.

The update also introduces a slightly tweaked Macintosh HD icon, removing the ports and holes that made it to macOS Tahoe 26.

Finally, macOS Tahoe 26.1 updates the Apple TV app icon, introducing the first hints of Apple’s promised new, more vibrant design language alongside the Apple TV+ rebranding to simply Apple TV.

title: Apple releases iOS 26.1 for iPhone with these changes
snippet: Apple has officially released iOS 26.1 to all iPhone users. Here’s what changes are available to the iPhone in iOS 26.1. more…
fullText:
Apple has officially released iOS 26.1 to all iPhone users. Here’s what changes are available to the iPhone in iOS 26.1.

Liquid Glass toggle

The biggest news from iOS 26.1 is the Liquid Glass toggle. Apple has added the option to choose between clear (the current design in iOS 26) and tinted. The tinted option changes the opacity level behind things like notifications and tab bars. Other Liquid Glass visual elements like optional clear app icons are still present.

The toggle is found in Settings > Display & Brightness > Liquid Glass on iPhone and iPad. The Mac also gains the toggle in Settings > Appearance > Liquid Glass, although the differences on macOS aren’t as apparent.

The new preference is in addition to accessibility settings that already exist like increase contrast, reduce transparency, and more.

Lock Screen Swipe

iOS 26.1 introduces a second toggle that may be welcomed by even more users. For the first time in years, it’s possible to disable the swipe to open Camera gesture on the iPhone lock screen.

The new toggle is found in Settings > Camera > Lock Screen Swipe to Open Camera.

The shortcut started as a swipe up gesture before later becoming a swipe from the right gesture in iOS 10. Starting with the iPhone X, Apple has included Lock Screen shortcuts for Flashlight and Camera by default.

Newer iPhones also include the Camera Control button, adding a third way to launch the Camera. Before that, the Action button introduced another method.

While the swipe option remains, including the ability to toggle it off in Settings can eliminate accidental swipes that unintentionally launch the Camera app.

More

More changes available in iOS 26.1 relate to Apple Intelligence, AirPods Live Translation, Apple TV, and iPad Slide Over.

Apple Intelligence gains support for Chinese (traditional), Danish, Dutch, Norwegian, Portuguese (Portugal), Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

AirPods Live Translation adds support for Chinese (Mandarin simplified and traditional), Italian, Japanese, and Korean. The feature launched with iOS 26 on AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods 4 with support for US and UK English, French, German, Portuguese (Brazil), and Spanish (Spain).

Apple is rebranding its streaming video service from Apple TV+ to just Apple TV. The rebrand is being accompanied by “a vibrant new identity,” according to Apple. The first sign of vibrancy comes with the new icon for the Apple TV app.

Settings app now includes a Local Capture section under General. The setting lets you change where Local Capture files are saved. You can also toggle Local Capture to only include audio.

iOS 26.1 also improves how alarms are dismissed with a Slide to Unlock interface, adds a swipe gesture for changing songs in the Music app, and much more.

Availability

iOS 26.1 is available for iPhone 11 and later, iPhone SE 2 and later, and iPhone Air.

title: Apple releases iPadOS 26.1, here’s everything new
snippet: Apple has released iPadOS 26.1, the latest noteworthy software update for iPad. Here’s everything new. more…
fullText:
Apple has released iPadOS 26.1, the latest noteworthy software update for iPad. Here’s everything new.

iPadOS 26.1’s new features include Slide Over’s return

iPadOS 26.1 brings the return of a key multitasking feature that had been removed from iPadOS 26.0.

Slide Over is back. Now available alongside the existing windowing system, you can designate an app’s window as your ‘Slide Over’ window. Just use the ‘Enter Slide Over’ option hiding behind the green traffic light window control.

Your Slide Over window can be easily hidden out of sight and brought back in when needed. Hitting the shortcut ‘Globe key + \’ on a hardware keyboard quickly reveals or hides it.

The biggest advantage of Slide Over is that it floats above all other windows, so you can work inside any other app and still keep Slide Over on-screen.

In iPadOS 18, Slide Over let you add multiple apps in a single stack for easy switching. That’s no longer available, as the feature now limits users to a single app at a time. But on the plus side, the Slide Over window can now be resized to your exact preferences—that wasn’t possible before.

Beyond Slide Over’s return, iPadOS 26.1 includes these new features:

Liquid Glass debuts an optional new ‘Tinted’ setting to increase opacity

Music lets you swipe on the MiniPlayer to change tracks

Apple Intelligence expands to eight new languages

Local Capture now offers a couple settings for audio/video recordings

Photos uses an updated playback scrubber for videos

plus some smaller UI and feature changes

Based on my beta experience, iPadOS 26.1 also runs smoother than 26.0 thanks to a variety of bug fixes and performance improvements.

You can download and install iPadOS 26.1 from Settings ⇾ General ⇾ Software Update on any iPad that supports iPadOS 26. A full list of compatible iPad hardware is available here.

title: Apple does launch new products in November, here’s when it happened last
snippet: Apple has long been expected to launch a new Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini 2, and AirTag 2 before the year ends. But it’s somewhat rare for the company to unveil new products in November or later. Here’s when it happened last. more…
fullText:
Apple has long been expected to launch a new Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini 2, and AirTag 2 before the year ends. But it’s somewhat rare for the company to unveil new products in November or later. Here’s when it happened last.

Apple’s last November product unveilings were in 2020

If you’ve followed Apple for long, you know that the company tends to launch new products in September every year and often October too.

What’s not so common is November or December launches.

Occasionally products will be released in the last couple months of the year that had been announced earlier. For example, last year’s M4 Macs were announced in October but shipped in November. And the 2019 Mac Pro officially launched in December but had been unveiled much earlier.

If you’re eagerly awaiting a new Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini 2, and/or AirTag 2, what are the chances of product unveilings happening this month?

Based on Apple’s history, November launches seem unlikely, but certainly not impossible.

The last time Apple held a noteworthy product release late in the year was 2020, when the first M1 Macs were unveiled on November 10. That same year, AirPods Max debuted via a December press release. 

These are pretty prominent examples—the Macs especially. But it is hard to use 2020 as an example of something that might happen again, for obvious reasons.

Looking further back, the year prior Apple debuted the 16-inch MacBook Pro on November 13, 2019.

That 2019 launch is perhaps the best recent example of a late-year release, since the M1 Macs and AirPods Max may very well have had their releases disrupted by COVID-related delays.

If Apple does plan to launch any or all of the rumored three products this year, we’ll almost certainly hear about them this week or next.

Though the rumored November 12 Apple Store overnight is likely related to holiday refreshes, Apple could always roll out the new products that day too.

fullText:
With the update rolling out today, Mac users will have 38 color options to customize their WhatsApp chats, like on the iPhone version. Here’s how it works.

Multiple preset and customizable options available

As spotted by WABetaInfo, the latest WhatsApp update for Mac adds a new customization setting that lets users choose from 38 color options for their chats, bringing feature parity with the iOS version of the app. This includes 22 preset options, as well as customizable color and brightness settings.

As usual, the future will slowly be rolled out to all users in the coming weeks, but you can check if you have it under Settings > Chats.

Here’s WABetaInfo on the new feature:

“Just like in WhatsApp Messenger, these themes automatically adjust the message bubble and background colors to create a consistent visual style. Users can also upload their own images as wallpapers, apply themes globally or to individual chats, and even combine solid colors with subtle design elements.”

They also note that themes don’t sync between devices, which in practice means that users can set one color scheme for a specific chat on the Mac, and another color scheme for that same chat on the iPhone.

title: Apple’s new original podcast tells an ‘unbelievable true story’
snippet: Apple has announced “Adrift”, an eight-part original podcast premiering on Apple Podcasts on November 10. Here’s what to expect. more…
fullText:
Apple has announced “Adrift”, an eight-part original podcast premiering on Apple Podcasts on November 10. Here’s what to expect.

Adrift premieres on November 10

As detailed by Apple, Adrift tells the story of the Robertsons, “a young British family whose dream to sail around the world becomes a fight for survival”.

In addition to a cinematic sound design and a “searing original score,” Adrift is hosted by Becky Milligan, who spent more than two decades at the BBC before joining Blanchard House as a producer and host. This is the third podcast collaboration between Blanchard House and Apple.

Here’s Apple on the new show:

“With immersive audio, first-person accounts and exclusive interviews revealing never-before-heard details, ‘Adrift’ takes listeners inside the Robertsons’ extraordinary journey, following parents Dougal and Lyn, their teenage children Douglas and Anne, and 12-year-old twins Sandy and Neil, as they find themselves hundreds of miles from land with no radio, few supplies and sharks circling. Stranded in the vast emptiness of the ocean, they must rely on ingenuity, instinct and one another to survive. But even surrounded by danger, the greatest challenges they face may come from within.”

The trailer for Adrift is already up on Apple Podcasts, and you can listen to it here.

If you’re an Apple TV subscriber, you can connect your subscription to Apple Podcasts and get all episodes on November 10. If not, you’ll be able to listen to the first three episodes on the same date, with new episodes being made available weekly through December 15.

title: MagSafe Monday: Anker Zolo Wireless Charger delivers Qi2-certified 15W MagSafe charging for iPhone
snippet: MagSafe charging docks are great for desks or nightstands, but sometimes a simple cable or pad is all you want to travel with. fullText:
MagSafe charging docks are great for desks or nightstands, but sometimes a simple cable or pad is all you want to travel with. The new Anker Zolo Wireless Charger takes that idea and gives it a boost with Qi2 support for 15W fast charging. It’s compact, affordable, and built for people who want MagSafe charging for low cost.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Build quality and design

The Anker Zolo Wireless Charger feels solid despite its small size. The actual puck is thicker than Apple’s, but not by much. It’s a simple MagSafe-style pad that sticks securely to the back of your iPhone or AirPods with strong magnets, so alignment is always snappy. The five-foot cable is really nice for traveling. I hate using the AC ports that most hotels include on the lamps so I choose the one on the wall, but then my iPhone has to stay on the floor. With a five-foot cord, I am in goos shape.

On the other end of the cord is USB-C, but It doesn’t include a power adapter. You’ll need to pair it with a 20W or higher power brick, you’ll get the full 15W charging speed. It’s lightweight, easy to pack, and the included cable tie keeps it neat and organized in your bag.

Is this the perfect travel charger?

There is something nice about keeping your travel setup simple. Just a wall adapter and a single MagSafe cord that works for both your iPhone and AirPods. The Anker Zolo Wireless Charger fits anywhere and goes anywhere. It is small enough to toss in a bag, yet perfect for the airport, hotel, etc. Traveling is when the five-foot cord comes in really handy

Because it supports Qi2, you get fast 15W charging speeds as long as you bring your own adapter and your iPhone supports. That is the tradeoff for keeping it low cost, but I have plenty of USB-C adaptors already.

Wrap up on the Anker Zolo Wireless Charger

The Anker Zolo Wireless Charger is a great MagSafe charger if you want a simple, travel-friendly option without the Apple price tag. It charges fast, stays cool, and the braied cable makes it more flexible than other otptions. You can easily use it at your desk, on your nightstand, or while traveling without feeling like you are carrying extra gear. If you want a reliable MagSafe charger that gets the job done without taking up space, this is an easy recommendation.

You can buy it from Amazon or directly from Anker.

title: Apple TV’s Pluribus is ‘riveting,’ ‘dazzling piece of entertainment’ per critic
snippet: Pluribus is a new TV show from Breaking Bad’s creator that premieres later this week on Apple TV. And a roundup of recent previews of the show, including one from a noteworthy critic, make it sound very much like a can’t-miss series. more…
fullText:
Pluribus is a new TV show from Breaking Bad’s creator that premieres later this week on Apple TV. And a roundup of recent previews of the show, including one from a noteworthy critic, make it sound very much like a can’t-miss series.

New Pluribus details emerge ahead of Apple TV premiere this week

This Friday, November 7, the first two episodes of Pluribus arrive on Apple TV. For those especially eager, the show technically drops at 9:00p.m. Eastern / 6:00p.m. Pacific on Thursday the 6th.

Though full reviews are embargoed until then, a growing number of publications have offered in-depth previews that tease a show well worth watching. No surprise considering creator Vince Gilligan’s resume.

For example, today at Rolling Stone, critic Alan Sepinwall wrote:

Pluribus has a reported budget of $15 million per episode, five times more than what the average Breaking Bad cost…Without a big star, without a familiar title, and with a premise that Gilligan wanted kept under wraps until the Nov. 7 premiere, Apple TV+ is gambling a lot of money that merely saying they have a new series from the creator of Breaking Bad will be enough to draw people in. 

“When you put it that way, you kind of scared me,” says Gilligan. 

He shouldn’t be scared. Pluribus is a dazzling piece of entertainment. It takes advantage of everything Gilligan learned about patient storytelling with Breaking Bad and Saul, then combines it with the high-concept ambition of X-Files, as well as the visual flair Gilligan has developed as a director on all his shows. Though the plot involves every person on the planet, the focus is often entirely on Carol, as Gilligan relies on all the things he realized Seehorn could do — tragedy, slapstick, and sheer screen presence — during her time playing attorney Kim Wexler on Saul. There are long stretches where we’re just watching Carol struggle through various tasks, like digging a grave. And it’s riveting. 

Adding to these words of praise, Sepinwall also writes on his Substack that, Stranger Things possibly aside, he considers Pluribus “the big TV event of the rest of the year.”

Vince Gilligan has done a lot of press over the last week, sharing tidbits on everything from Pluribus’ origins and genre to how long the show might run.

Gilligan told The Verge that, while he had wanted to return to sci-fi after his previous run on The X-Files, with Pluribus he “didn’t make a conscious decision to make another sci-fi show. Instead, “I realized there was no other way to explain the happenings other than science fiction.”

Pluribus is already picked up for a second season, but Gilligan told Polygon he has plans for at least a third as well—assuming the series is a hit.

“If you held a gun to my head, I would say three seasons. At least I would hope for three seasons…I said that in the early days of Breaking Bad…and then it turned out to be six, which was great. There turned out to be more story than I thought was possible. So maybe that’ll be the case here. Maybe it won’t be. I don’t know.”
